title: Debugging DNS queries with strace and tcpdump
author: Julia Evans
snippet: Last week I was debugging a weird DNS issue where some queries were timing out. I used strace to trace the system calls and tcpdump to capture the actual packets on the wire. Here is what I found and how I fixed it.
body:
Last week I was debugging a weird DNS issue where some queries were timing out. I used strace to trace the system calls and tcpdump to capture the actual packets on the wire. Here is what I found and how I fixed it.

First, I ran strace on the process:

```
strace -e trace=network -p 12345
```

This showed me that the process was making DNS queries to 8.8.8.8 but the responses were being dropped. Looking at tcpdump output:

```
tcpdump -i eth0 port 53
```

I could see the queries going out but responses coming back with the truncation bit set. The issue was that our firewall was blocking TCP DNS fallback. The fix was straightforward: allow TCP port 53 through the firewall.

Here is the iptables rule I added:

```
iptables -A INPUT -p tcp --dport 53 -j ACCEPT
```

After that, everything worked. The root cause was that our DNSSEC responses were too large for UDP (over 512 bytes) and needed TCP fallback.

References:
- RFC 5966: DNS Transport over TCP
- https://www.isc.org/docs/dns-troubleshooting.pdf
